$comment: THE fork ledger. apps/community-editor is a COPY of apps/editor (source-available offline build).
Every intentional difference from upstream is one
entry here with a written reason. check-upstream-drift.mjs FAILS on:
(a) a file that differs with no entry  -> an accidental divergence,
(b) an entry that no longer applies    -> a stale exemption, which is how a fork silently
A path ending in /** matches everything under that prefix.
node_modules/ holds ONLY esbuild, copied from upstream so tools/build-bundle.mjs can minify. It is in ignore[], not entries[], because the walker never descends into it.
.impeccable/ is a design-lint hook cache written by the tooling, not source. Ignored rather than recorded, like node_modules and dist.

Cloud transcribers and their helpers deleted; local-only model list; transformers.js loads from vendor/ instead of the /api/cdn bridge; the modal lost the controls only a cloud engine could answer, and it now refuses with a sentence when the page was opened as a file (the model cannot be read from disk there).

The rnnoise WASM URL pointed at rnnoise-wasm@1.0.0, which does not exist on npm (only 0.0.1-security), so it has always 404d and denoise has always used its fallback gate. Now null, so no request is made; setWasmUrl stays for a packager who has a real build.
FACEMESH_CDN documented: the face tracker is hidden alpha, so its model is deliberately not vendored, and vendoring is required before it is ever made visible.

What the build is, what it deliberately is not, how to run it, and the one thing a local-only app must say out loud: clearing site data deletes every project.

loadGoogleFont no longer downloads a non-vendored family by default. The 16 bundled families resolve locally; anything else is opt-in (cc_allow_google_fonts) and RESOLVES rather than rejects, so a missing webfont falls back to a system face instead of taking down the caller.
The upload-ceiling probe (/api/account/rate-limits) is skipped when CCEdition.serverless: it was a guaranteed 404 on every boot and the module already has a default ceiling.

R7. The ElevenLabs sound and music GENERATION tabs are DELETED (batch generator, per-provider settings, setup modal, the spends-credit banner, the vendor endpoint). They ran on the pooled key through /api/proxy, so unlike the stock SEARCH providers beside them no user key could stand in. _stockAiIsAi survives as the predicate at the two entry points, which now show the shared AI card. The stock SEARCH providers are untouched and run on the user own key.

Two fixes. The file:// banner pointed at pnpm dev and localhost:3000/editor, neither of which exists here. And the file: guard RETURNED before the CC_BUNDLED branch, so a double-clicked page mounted zero modules: a bundle is two tags, not a fetch, so it now loads from file:// and skips the two fetches (manifest.json, bundle.meta.json) that only a server needs. THIRD fix (2026-08-20): LIB_INTEGRITY names LOCAL paths instead of jsDelivr and cdnjs. Upstream can reach a CDN because it runs beside apps/web; this edition promises to work with no network, and "export to PDF" failing silently offline is that promise broken in the most ordinary place. Verified against the SRI hashes upstream had already pinned (tools/vendor-cdn-libs.mjs).
"/" serves index.prod.html when it exists. index.html fetches 299 modules one at a time and is the development page; the bundle is what ships.

The development page: every module loaded separately so a source edit shows on reload with no rebuild. It is upstream index.html, renamed, because in an offline build the file people double-click must be the one that RUNS. R8 adds the core/account.js script tag; core/ files are not covered by the module bundle, so a new one needs a tag here or it silently never loads.
Reads index.dev.html and writes index.html (upstream reads index.html and writes index.prod.html). The bundle owns the obvious name here.
The BUSL-1.1 text with its four-year change licence intact. Upstream has no LICENSE file at all; this edition cannot be published without one.

GSAP replaced with anime.js (MIT). GSAP is free of charge but not an OSI licence and this build is redistributed. It was used in exactly this one file, and only to tween numbers on proxy objects, so one _tw helper covers all nine call sites; it also owns the two unit conversions (GSAP counts seconds, anime.js milliseconds) and translates stored GSAP easing names. The gsap.ticker render loop became rAF, and the zoom branch lost a fromTo plus a set that the proxy tween overwrote every frame anyway.

Proof for the GSAP removal: real Chromium, real file:// URL, drives an anime.js proxy tween of the exact shape deck-ui now uses. A wrong easing name or a missed seconds-to-milliseconds conversion shows up as a number rather than an opinion.

Proof for the GSAP removal on a REAL deck: builds 11 slides, opens the presenter, presses ArrowRight and samples the incoming stage computed style every frame, per preset, against the property that preset actually drives. It measures DURATION as well as movement, because a missed seconds-to-milliseconds conversion still fires the completion callback.

The element-animation half. Wraps fabric.StaticCanvas to get a handle on the presenter own canvas and reads OBJECT properties frame by frame. Reading a canvas pixel instead was the first attempt and proved nothing: two colours at one point means the slide changed, not that anything animated.

The social tiles are the THIRD ad surface (owner). Five of them called ExportManager.openSocial, which went with export/social-publish, so they answered with a red "Social sharing unavailable" error toast; the rest shared _shLink(), which here is a local file path nobody on the other end can open. Every tile now opens the social card instead, and Download in the same menu still works.

A dependency-free Chrome DevTools Protocol driver. This build is meant to be opened as a FILE, and neither available test tool could drive that: the shared playwright install vanished mid-session and the in-app browser renders a file:// page as a static snapshot. Both are tooling problems, and neither is a reason to test over http and call it proof. Needs only Node and the chromium already on disk, and deliberately does NOT pass --allow-file-access-from-files, which would give the page powers a real user does not have.

THE proof, run on a double-clicked index.html: boot, zero cross-origin requests, IndexedDB, the three ad surfaces, and a save that survives a full reload. Replaces the playwright probes as the one that must pass before a release.

Community-editor locale proof: opens the generated file build, switches every requested locale through Settings > Preferences, checks localized guidance and dynamic text, and fails on page or console errors.
Visible-surface locale audit: crawls the file build after rail/flyout/settings navigation and reports unchanged or Turkish-character UI text per requested locale.

R0. The code is source-available; the name remains protected. A modified fork must rebrand. Cheapest and most effective brake on a competing fork.
R0. The CLA requirement stated before the first outside pull request, plus the house rules that are not style preferences (no network request, no ghost UI, no localStorage).
R0. States the real threat model: no server, no account, everything on the user machine, stock keys in plain form. Without that, half the reports would be about the design.
R0. dist/ and index.html are deliberately NOT ignored: the bundle IS the product and somebody who clones this must be able to double-click it.
R1. 87 MB of ambient audio with ZERO references anywhere in the tree, and only three distinct tracks copied ten times.

R1. 167 MB for no visible difference: the module own measurement records fp16 scoring an IoU of 1.000 against it. The Quality tier went with it, because a radio list with one option is a control nobody can use.

R1. One tier. TIERS has a single entry, _autoTier is gone, and the consent modal renders an informational row instead of a radio when there is only one tier (it still renders radios if a tier is ever added back, so the list decides rather than a hardcoded shape).

R2 then R8. It is the setup wizard AND the launch gate. Owner decision 2026-08-15: registration is required and asked on EVERY launch until the install has an account. "Later" walks past it for that session and writes nothing that suppresses the next one; there is no "do not show again", by decision. A returning visitor gets the account screen ALONE, not the five-screen wizard again. It waits on BOTH CCLocalStore.ready and CCAccount.ready: the first resolves to "no previous work" on a slow disk, the second to "signed out" for somebody who registered last week. Screen 2 is still why the wizard exists. Escape does not close it.

R3 then R8. It shipped inert (ENDPOINT null, opt-in default off). D4 was answered ON 2026-08-15 and the destination is the member log that already exists under :3001 users, not a new table. It is therefore DISCLOSED rather than asked about: the wizard and Settings > Account both print the payload in words. Seven fields, and accountId is the only conditional one. The ACCOUNT ID goes in the body, never the token: a credential in a POST body is a credential in every access log on the way.

R5. Wiring to the Electron shell, and nothing at all when window.CCDesktop is absent, so the browser build is unchanged. Open and Save go through the existing .ccproj reader and writer. R8: the editor top bar becomes the window title bar (the shell has no native frame and no menu bar; it used to stack three rows and print "File" twice), and the four things the native menu did are REHOMED into the editor's own File and Help menus. The strip reserved for the OS window buttons is CSS env(titlebar-area-*), never a measured JS value: the JS version read correctly on one run and returned visible:false on the next.
R2. The setup wizard must be reachable again from Settings > About; somebody who skipped it otherwise has no way back to the one screen explaining where their work is stored.

R2 proof on a real file:// page: appears once on a fresh profile, screen 2 carries the warning, telemetry defaults off, Escape does not close it, choices persist, a second boot does not show it, Settings reopens it.

R7. AI mode and PRODUCTS mode both render the ad card; EXCEL is untouched and stays live, because it is the half that works offline. The Products choice card lost its disabled state: upstream greys it out when the catalogue is unreachable, and a greyed-out button that never explains itself is exactly the ghost UI this build exists not to ship. Products steps 2 and 3 are the SHARED wizard (Excel uses them too) and are untouched. _bbAiSys lost its BUILTIN_SKILLS lookup; the rest of the AI block is unreachable and recorded here rather than carved out piecemeal.

R7. The scope switch is SPLIT: "Bu proje" is local and untouched, "All projects" is the org-wide read model over /api/tags/entities and now shows the works card instead of an empty grid or a bare "Failed to load." that explains nothing.

R8. THE account reader and writer. A device-code flow (RFC 8628) because a cookie session cannot reach this build: file:// sends Origin null and the desktop shell is on app://, which is not https, so the session cookie is neither stored nor sent, and a redirect flow has nowhere to return to. Renders the shared sign-in panel for both hosts so the six states exist once. Sign-out clears locally FIRST, then tells the server best-effort.

R8 (D7 answered yes). Upgrades an ALREADY-PAINTED lockSurface card to a served creative; the static card is the floor and a failed request changes nothing. Overlay formats are REFUSED outright, not handled: the hosted editor measured an unpainted full-screen overlay capturing the whole viewport and looking exactly like a frozen app, and reimplementing that fix in a build nobody operates is three chances to get it wrong. javascript:/data: links and unknown placements are dropped by the sanitiser.

R8. Settings > Account: the way OUT. This build asks for registration at every launch, so there has to be a door in the other direction and it has to be obvious. It renders CCAccount’s panel rather than a second copy of the flow states, and it states where the session is kept, which differs between the file build and the desktop app because the fact differs.

R8. THE registration wizard, FULL SCREEN, shown before anything else while signed out. Its steps are NOT written here: they come from GET /api/community/wizard, which serves the wizard the owner authors at :3001 (Forms > Signup (Community Editor)), so editing it there changes this app on the next launch with no release. Falls back to the last definition seen, then to a built-in screen, so it is never a dead end offline. "Later" always exists and writes nothing that suppresses the next launch. Renders the same WizardStep vocabulary as the website (cards/list/fields/content, showWhen, required, skippable).

R8. Drives the real file:// build against a running server and photographs the registration wizard, because "the wizard renders" is a claim about how something looks. It found the missing input listener: the probe set field values without firing `input`, Next stayed disabled and the click did nothing, which is exactly what a person typing would have hit.

The dika studio rename (owner, 2026-08-15), kept as a script rather than done by hand because the dangerous part is what it must NOT touch. It replaces  CardCraft  and  CARDCRAFT  only; `_` being a word character is what makes cardcraft_autosave, CardCraftFontLibrary, CARDCRAFT_CUSTOM_PROPS and the .cardcraft extension untouched BY CONSTRUCTION. It counts 22 protected identifiers before and after the write and exits non-zero if any count moved. 178 replacements, 107 files, zero protected drift.

One-word fix with a real bug behind it: `initIconRail` bound a click to EVERY `.rail-item`, and `#settings-btn` has no `data-tab`, so pressing Settings also called `openFlyout(undefined)` and left the left panel OPEN AND EMPTY with the Settings item highlighted (`undefined === undefined`). Selector narrowed to `.rail-item[data-tab]`. The bug predates this fork; the settings screen covered it, so it was only visible on the way out.

The settings screen is `inset: 0` and its close button sits top-right, which in the desktop shell is exactly under the OS-drawn minimise / maximise / close buttons: reported as "the X disappeared". It now reserves the same strip the top bar does, through `env(titlebar-area-width)`, so both measure it identically and the browser build keeps its original 20px through the fallback.
Community i18n surface fix: shortcut categories and action labels use CCI18n, the infinite-canvas category is English in source, and physical key names remain marked as non-translatable identifiers.

THE translation runtime (docs/dika-studio-i18n-tasks.md). RULES.md deferred the editor to "its own approved project" because it is ES5 with no bundler; this is its foundation. The key is the ENGLISH SOURCE STRING, so a module can be translated on its own and an untranslated string renders as correct English rather than as an id. Dictionaries are .js injected as a <script>, never .json fetched: a file:// page cannot fetch a local file. Switching language never reloads, because a reload throws away unsaved work.

Translation dictionaries, one .js per locale calling CCI18n.add (a script tag is the only way this build can read a local file). Turkish is seeded with 44 strings out of 3,669 unique; the key is the English source verbatim, and an identifier - object key, enum value, event name, CSS class, storage key - never appears here.

Twenty-nine screenshot drivers for the COMMERCIAL marketing site (:3002) and admin console (:3001), copied in with the fork. They point at hosts this edition has no relationship with, hardcode the build machine home directory, and two of them (_shot_auth_e2e) show how to sign in with the DEV-only agent account. Nothing in the community editor calls them. Removed 2026-08-20 before the repository went public; backup at D:/Cursor/cartcraft-community-scripts-backup-20260820-090345.zip.
A probe against the commercial site on :3002. Same reason as the _shot_ drivers.
Marked TEMP by its own first line and tests CCTags.reconcileFromServer(), which merges tags FROM A SERVER. There is no content API in this edition, so it asserts a behaviour that cannot happen here.
Marked TEMP by its own first line and reads apps/editor/modules/... - a path OUTSIDE this repository, so it could only ever fail once published.

The CORS relay for the commercial standalone editor (:8200 -> :3456). This build reaches two hosts of its own and the stock providers direct on the user key, so it relays nothing. The root copy at scripts/qdrant-proxy.js is the one launch.json starts; this was a duplicate.

Drives /api/assets and /api/stock/save - PANEL endpoints that do not exist in this edition - and reads apps/web/.env.local by absolute path for the DEV agent account. Broken and disclosive in equal measure.

The 222 emoji this panel offers, vendored as SVG. Upstream draws them from jsDelivr, which means the emoji panel is 222 network requests and renders nothing offline. CC-BY 4.0 attribution travels in LICENSE.txt beside them.
